title: Macaroni Cheese
subtitle: Baked pasta in creamy cheese sauce with a golden crust
excerpt: The American comfort-food icon: macaroni coated in a rich, sharp cheddar béchamel sauce, turned into a baking dish, topped with more cheese and breadcrumbs, and baked until the top is golden and the inside is bubbling and creamy.

recipe.sourceNotes: Macaroni and cheese has been eaten in Europe since at least the fourteenth century (the Liber de Coquina documents a dish of pasta layered with cheese). Thomas Jefferson is often credited with bringing it to America after encountering pasta in Italy during his time as Ambassador to France, and a recipe appears in Mary Randolph's The Virginia Housewife (1824). The baked, breadcrumb-topped version became the American standard by the mid-nineteenth century. The béchamel-based sauce (milk thickened with a roux of butter and flour) became the dominant method in the twentieth century; before that, the dish was often made by layering pasta and cheese without a sauce. The key to the sauce is getting it thick enough that it does not become watery when baked: the pasta releases starch into the sauce as it bakes, so the sauce should be thicker than you want the final dish.

content.text: Make the cheese sauce thicker than seems right; it loosens in the oven. Undercook the pasta by 2 minutes before adding to the sauce: it will finish cooking in the oven. A mixture of sharp mature cheddar and a small amount of gruyere or emmental gives both flavour and melt.

Heat the oven to 200°C / fan 180°C / gas 6. Cook the pasta in well-salted water for 2 minutes less than the packet says. Drain and set aside. Make the sauce: melt the butter in a pan, add the flour, and stir over medium heat for 1 minute. Add the milk gradually, whisking constantly, and cook for 5 minutes until thick and smooth.
Remove from the heat. Add most of the cheddar and all the gruyere, the mustard, cayenne, salt, and pepper. Stir until the cheese has melted. Combine with the pasta.

Pour into a buttered baking dish. Top with the remaining cheddar and the breadcrumbs. Bake for 20 to 25 minutes until golden on top and bubbling at the edges. Leave to stand for 5 minutes before serving.
